questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and gaining a deeper understanding of the culture and daily life of the everyday Japanese people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't always so easy because most of the information we received were in Japanese and there was only one staff who spoke english at my university campus so she was often quite busy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In-dorm assistant tutor. They helped with everyday tasks and more important things such as post and bank etc. They were friendly and very helpful but they could only speak Japanese and minimal English so that was a challenge in itself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Nice modern Dormitory called Mitra-kan, 2min from campus (would highly recommend). There was also an all boys dormitory and another unisex dormitory called Kokusai house.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Several canteens, convenience stores, and restaurants/cafes around campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Go with the pricier option, the other ones are cheaper for a reason.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Convoluted and slow

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Minimal

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We were not properly informed about what our extra curricular classes would entail. We were told that the classes taught in Japanese would be easy for beginners and are specifically made for exchange students, and we were encouraged to take them. In reality the teachers could not speak a word of english, they spoke standard Japanese in standard speed like they would normally. DO not take the extra curricular courses in Japanese unless you can somewhat understand at a higher level like JLPT N3 and up. Definitely not for beginners.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early and ask around. Contact the exchange university for questions, they usually know more.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was quite high, it was challenging as the language courses were taught in Japanese, which I was not used to previously but it definitely paid off. The workload is often overwhelming, there is a midterm test and final test, but there are also pop quizzes every other week or so. Plus homework on top of that.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More serious and tighter schedule, we were learning Japanese at an academic university level with topics such as climate change and AI.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Japanese language, Japanese pop culture, Japanese religion, Japanese martial arts & theatre

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese pop culture and language courses of course

questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is cheaper than Denmark but it definitely racks up if you go out every day. 
Taking a weekend-trip to another prefecture is not as cheap as I thought. 
You will spend more money than you think. Save up a lot more than you initially planned. Probably double that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
!!Important 
If you arrive in the autumn semester then good luck getting into any club/sports club, I tried many times with many different clubs/circles but they only accept new members in spring time.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there's several cultural exchange social activities at the campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get a language partner, go to cultural exchange events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore other prefectures, go to flea markets and visit temples/shrines. Also walk everywhere, you'll find unique places and those are definitely some of my best memories.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Without realising it, you'll quickly get used to the local culture and language. Took me about 2 weeks to fully adjust. Don't be worried if you can't understand what they're saying, you'll get used to it after some time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's like talking with a shy wall but it's not impossible. You have to take initiative and go for it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their timidness and reluctance to approach one or take initiative in social settings

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The order and cleanliness, also how everyone is quiet. You feel safe wherever you go, even more so than in Denmark. Japan is aesthetically very beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Save up a lot of money, go explore at any chance you get, take initiative and try new things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Immersing myself in the language and culture. It was a valuable experience that can't be replaced with anything else.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness. It felt excruciatingly long and at the same time very short.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
